approach: In crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, an item's second failure now ends as `ItemEnd::Failed(Failure)`. `Failure { reason, shared: Option<String> }` is built where the failure arises, and `shared` is Some only for a cause that is not a verdict on the item. Three origins are shared: (a) a run or read that ended in an error with no outcome (`Run.outcome == None`, the Err arm of `RealSteps::run` 3562 and `RealSteps::read` 3510), (b) a run that ended `Failed` with a reason that `athena_core::disk::StopCause::of` reads as an environment cause (LowDisk, CheckTimeout, ProducerAuth, UsageLimit, OtherEnvironment), and (c) a landing that errored, not one that reported pull-request state. For (c) a new `Landing::Error(String)` variant is produced only by the `Err` arm of `landing_from_report` (3056). The `Ok` arm (3052) stays `NotLanded`, because red CI is a verdict on that item. Rejected, TimedOut, a Failed outcome with a work reason, the critic and planning-cap verdicts, 'checks failed after rebase' and pull-request-state landings are `shared: None`. The key for a named environment cause is the StopCause kind. Otherwise it is the detail with names, job ids and numbers masked. `Drain::finish` does the check and insert in one lock section. If an earlier different item holds the same key it calls `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item))` and notes both items. Otherwise it notes and calls `pass_over`, like Paused and Skipped. Tests script `Run` and `Landing` values on the doubles. Landing values are built with the production `landing_from_report`, made `pub`, so the tests use the exact text the drain sees.

decisions.choice: Classify by origin, reusing the existing environment classifier. `run_job`'s `other` arm sets `shared` when `other.is_none()`, or when `other == Some(Failed)` and `athena_core::disk::StopCause::of(&run.reason).is_environment()` (disk.rs 388-415, the same test as run/mod.rs 598 and scope_guard.rs 547). The key for LowDisk, CheckTimeout, ProducerAuth and UsageLimit is the StopCause kind (Debug text), so two items with different detail text but the same 429 match. For OtherEnvironment, and for no-outcome errors, the key is the normalized detail.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. Usage-limit and expired-login failures are the 'environment / Athena itself' causes the request names. The code already classifies them, so the open question about Failed outcomes is dropped. A Failed run with a Work reason is a failure of that item and only pauses it.

rejected.option: Treat every Failed outcome as shared
rejected.why: A producer crash on its own task is Failed with a Work reason, and it is per item.

rejected.option: Treat every finished outcome as per item (previous plan)
rejected.why: Usage-limit and expired-login stops would cost two runs per queued item until budget or job limit.

rejected.option: Compare reason text for all failures
rejected.why: Fixed verdict sentences such as 'the critic rejected the plan' would match across unrelated items, which is the reported fault.

decisions.choice: Add `Landing::Error(String)` (pub enum, drain.rs 467) and return it only from the `Err` arm of `landing_from_report`. `Drain::land` (1696) handles it like NotLanded: it prints, writes `st.jobs[at].landing = "not landed: <why>"`, and returns `LandStep::NotLanded { host_error: Some(why) }`. `LandStep::NotLanded` (1295) becomes a struct variant, and `NotLanded(why)` gives `host_error: None`. The after-rebase recheck (1648-1651) returns `host_error: None`. `RealSteps::land` (3607 `other => other`) passes the new variant through unchanged. `attempts` turns a Some host_error into `shared: failure_key(..)`. Make `landing_from_report` `pub`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Text at 3052 is a fixed sentence (`pull request N is Open, checks Some(Red); ...`), so a red check is a verdict on the item's own change. Only the gh Err (3056) is a host or Athena fault. The split is made at the place that knows which one it is, not by reading text. Making the function `pub` lets tests build both forms with production code (finding 3).

rejected.option: Keep NotLanded as one variant and compare text
rejected.why: Two red-CI items would produce the same masked key and stop the batch, which is the reported fault.
Changes the tuple variant in every constructor (drain.rs 5188, tests/drain.rs 246). A separate variant leaves existing NotLanded constructors valid.

rejected.option: Treat the after-rebase recheck failure as shared
rejected.why: `Steps::rerun_checks` detail is the item's own check output. It is a verdict, so it is per item.

decisions.choice: For a read: `RunStep::Failed` built at 1504 gets `shared` only when `read.job.is_none() && read.error.is_some() && !read.held`, the Err arm at 3510, and when the error is not the no-capability sentence. A reader's own report (job Some with error, runnable false) is per item.
decisions.reason: An `athena.go` Err is a host or Athena error. A reading that says no capability fits is a verdict on the request.

rejected.option: Treat any read error as shared
rejected.why: Reader-reported errors with a job present are about that request.

decisions.choice: Key helper `failure_key(text, names) -> Option<String>`: lower-case, split on whitespace, trim edge punctuation, mask whole tokens equal to a name (item or retry job), a job-id-shaped token or an all-digit token, re-join with single spaces. An empty result is None and never matches. `State.failures: Vec<(String, String)>` holds shared keys only. Check and insert happen in one `self.st()` section in `finish`, and `set_stop` and `note` are called after the lock is dropped.
decisions.reason: Host and run errors embed the job name or a number, so masking makes the same cause match. Whole-token matching avoids corrupting short names such as `a`. One lock section means two concurrent workers (`drain_concurrent`) cannot both miss each other.

decisions.choice: Keep `Report::failed_item` for the shared-cause stop only (the later item), and name the earlier item in a note. Keep the display prefix 'repeated failure: item X failed twice' and append 'for a cause shared with an earlier item (see notes)'. Leave the item in `report.queued`, untried again this run (`State.begun` and `tried`).
decisions.reason: No new Report field, so the JSON shape and the existing prefix assertions are unchanged. This matches how Paused and Skipped behave, and no pause record is written (the scope guard is out of scope).

rejected.why: Changes the serialized report for detail a note already carries.
Touches the scope guard, out of scope.

In `attempts` keep `let mut last = Failure::default()`. On `RunStep::Failed { failure, .. }` set `last = failure`. Replace the `ItemEnd::Failed` arm of `finish`: in one `self.st()` section, if `failure.shared` is Some(key), look for an entry for a different item with the same key, then push (item, key). If matched, after dropping the lock call `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item.job.clone()))` and note 'item X failed twice for the same cause as item Y: reason; the run stops'. risks.risk: Two unrelated verdicts with the same fixed sentence (critic reject, planning cap) are taken as a shared cause.
risks.mitigation: Only no-outcome errors, Failed runs with an environment StopCause, and `Landing::Error` can be shared. A rejection, a timeout, a Failed run with a Work reason, a pull-request-state NotLanded and the after-rebase recheck are never shared. Unit tests and the criterion 2 and 3 controls run this through the drain.

risks.risk: An `Err` from `athena.go` or a run may be item-specific (for example a refused request), so two such items would stop the batch.
risks.mitigation: A refused request or no-capability reading comes back as `Ok` with `runnable: false` or as a Rejected outcome, not as an Err. The Err arms (3510, 3562) carry host and Athena errors, as their code shows. A stop is the conservative result and names both items in a note.

risks.risk: A true shared cause is missed because its text embeds per-item data (paths, counts), so the batch pauses items one at a time.
risks.mitigation: Named environment causes (429, 401, low disk, check timeout) are keyed by the StopCause kind, not text. Other keys mask names, job ids and numbers. A miss only pauses more items, each with a visible note, and the budget and job limit bound the run.

risks.risk: Tests could pass by relying on the stub's own text rather than on production classification.
risks.mitigation: The doubles return scripted `Run` and `Landing` values only. Landings are built with the production `landing_from_report`. The control cases show that verdict-shaped failures continue.

risks.risk: The Before::RepeatedFailure seeding runs two workers with timing waits, and a second failing item changes the order.
risks.mitigation: Reseed with `errors: ["bad","bad2"]` and `wait_for ('new','end bad2-retry')`; the loop already waits for the entry and then 150 ms for the stop to be stored. Keep the asserted row counts and run the whole file.

risks.risk: A failed item stays in `report.queued`, so the next `athena drain` retries it and a permanently failing item repeats across runs.
risks.mitigation: This matches how Paused and Skipped items behave. The note says 'paused for this run'. A persistent pause would touch the scope guard, which is out of scope.

risks.risk: The new `Landing` variant and the `LandStep` and `RunStep::Failed` changes break matches elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: The compiler finds each one. The only matches on `Landing` and `LandStep` are in drain.rs. Test doubles only construct `Landing::Landed` and `NotLanded`, and both stay valid.
